cases.title: Late Fee After Hospitalization
cases.scenario_text:
[TO BE FINALIZED] You were hospitalized unexpectedly for a week. During that time, you missed a payment deadline and incurred a $50 late fee. You have the documentation of your hospitalization. The late fee policy says it can be waived for documented emergencies.

You can pay the $50 late fee immediately and avoid any further complications, or you can submit a dispute with your hospitalization documentation requesting a waiver. The dispute process takes 2-3 weeks and there's no guarantee it will be approved.

actions.label: Take no action
actions.description: Ignore for now (may result in additional penalties)

cases.title: CEO's Preferred Candidate
cases.scenario_text:
[TO BE FINALIZED] You're on a hiring committee for your team. You've interviewed six candidates. Before the committee meeting, your CEO calls and says one candidate is the daughter of a close friend, and asks you to "give her serious consideration."

She's qualified but clearly not the strongest candidate. You're up for a promotion that the CEO will decide. You can make your recommendation in the committee meeting.

actions.label: Abstain from recommendation
actions.description: Present all candidates neutrally without recommendation

cases.title: Faulty Power Bank
cases.scenario_text:
[TO BE FINALIZED] You bought a power bank online for $45. After two weeks, it stopped working. The return window is 30 days, so you're eligible for a refund.

However, you're also a frequent buyer from this seller (you've made 10+ purchases), and you've noticed they're a small business. The return process would require them to pay return shipping ($8) and they'd lose the sale.

You can afford the $45 loss without hardship.

actions.label: Return for refund
actions.description: Request refund through proper return process

actions.label: Keep the product
actions.description: Accept the loss and don't request refund

actions.label: Contact seller directly
actions.description: Reach out to discuss options before formal return

cases.title: Bonus Split
cases.scenario_text:
[TO BE FINALIZED] You received a $2,000 performance bonus. Your manager told you it was for your individual work on a project.

However, you know your colleague contributed significantly to the project's success, spending extra hours and solving critical problems. They did not receive a bonus, and you suspect it's because they're newer to the team and not yet eligible under company policy.

You could keep the full bonus (which you earned under company rules), or share some of it with your colleague.

actions.label: Share the bonus
actions.description: Give some of the bonus to your colleague

actions.label: Escalate to management
actions.description: Raise the issue that colleague should also be recognized
